Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: No evidence found of AI/analytics integrated into Tunisia's UXP interoperability platform or national data exchange. Tunisia has general AI strategy discussions but no confirmed AI deployment within data exchange operations.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Cited source (Cybernetica, Feb 2024) verified: confirms Tunisia's national interoperability platform (UXP, built on Estonia's X-Road) was piloted from 2023 with five ministries, but makes no mention of AI or analytics functionality. Fresh searches for newer evidence found: (1) a launch article (Mar 2024) describing the platform's functions as data-quality checks and instant document verification between administrations — administrative/rules-based checks, not AI/ML; (2) a May 2026 news report confirming Phase 1 completed in 2025 and a new contract (through end-2027) for Phase 2, scaling to all ministries, again with no mention of AI, fraud detection, or predictive analytics; (3) a July 2026 Cabinet meeting readout listing digitisation projects with no AI/analytics component named. No authoritative source describes an AI or analytics layer within Tunisia's data exchange. Original score of 0 (Unknown or n.a.) is confirmed rather than upgraded to '1=No', since absence of mention in progress reports is not the same as an explicit statement that no AI capability exists or is planned; genuine evidence is unavailable either way. Year updated to reflect the vintage of the newest sources reviewed.
revised_comments: No evidence is available that artificial intelligence is integrated into Tunisia's national data exchange (the UXP interoperability platform run by the Ministry of Communication Technologies) for data quality, fraud detection, or predictive analytics. Public accounts of the platform, including its 2025 Phase 1 completion and 2026 Phase 2 expansion contract, describe rules-based data verification and document exchange between ministries but do not reference any AI or machine-learning component. Tunisia has separate, general AI strategy discussions and a growing private-sector AI industry (banking, telecoms), but no confirmed link between these and the government data exchange system.
